meta.strategicSummary: At closure day 32 with Brent at $109.24, c rises to 0.90 reflecting both price-implied escalation and the structural removal of the UNSC military authorization path via Russian, Chinese, and French vetoes. m_effective remains 3.0 with bypass infrastructure intact. E* = 5 × [1 + 0.90 × (3.0−1)] = 14.0 in the Hormuz-only regime; the trap remains firmly active. Sr coverage sits at roughly 4% of the G+S threshold (18.78), meaning Iran's dominant strategy is unbroken. Ps has fallen to 5.5 following France's refusal to support military action — a permanent discontinuous drop — further eroding the security guarantee pillar. The UNSC veto is the most consequential structural event of this cycle: it forecloses collective enforcement, hardens mediator_risk to 0.75, and signals that the closure can persist without triggering a multilateral military response, deepening the equilibrium trap.
meta.mostSignificantEvent: Headline 1: Russia, China, and France blocking UNSC military authorization permanently removes the multilateral enforcement threat that could have altered Iran's dominant strategy calculus, constituting a -1 Ps event and a structural deepening of the closure trap.

paramNotes.dual_strait: Binary flag: 0 = Hormuz-only scenario; 1 = dual-strait activation (Hormuz + Bab-el-Mandeb via Houthi proxy). When 1, m switches from m_base to m_activated.
paramNotes.m_base: Geographic multiplier when only Hormuz is threatened (~20% global oil). Default 3.0.
paramNotes.m_activated: Geographic multiplier when both Hormuz and Bab-el-Mandeb (Houthi proxy) are simultaneously threatened (~30% global oil + Red Sea disruption). Default 4.75.
paramNotes.mediator_status: Binary flag: 1 = Qatar/Oman back-channel operative (sanctions-relief pathway open); 0 = mediator pathway closed (IRGC strike on Qatari/Omani assets or diplomatic rupture). When 0, Sr is gated — cannot rise regardless of diplomatic signals.
